newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch up on auction results.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch up on auction results.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened marginally higher on Wednesday on follow-through from late buying the previous session and lower-then-expected increases in primary rates.

"It's quiet, but there is demand. Not much fresh news, but we have some upward momentum and Cetes went up by less than expected, and that helps," a desk trader said. The leading IPC share index was up 2.41 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.06 percent, at 4,145.33.
Trading volume was moderate at 3.2 million shares.

Banco de Mexico placed bellwether 28-day Cetes at 20.43 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, a rise of 113 basis points since last week. This compared with an average forecast increase of 147 basis points in a previously conducted Reuters survey.
"There is some buying, by locals and foreigners, but not across the board. Several blue chips are flat or down," a floor trader said.
Dealers said the bourse failed to match early gains by the Dow Jones as market makers awaited U.S. data for signs of possible interest rate hikes in the near future.
The Dow Jones industrial average was meanwhile up 10.13 points at 7,549.40.
Retail stock Cifra contributed most to market gains, following an announced merger with Wal-Mart Store Inc last week.
"They're speculating on the share price at which the deal will be settled. They're buying at these levels, but they get cold feet at 14.00 pesos," a floor trader said.
Cifra B class shares were up 14 centavos to 13.46 pesos, although the C class was unchanged at 11.98 pesos.
The two share series, which are both included in the IPC, accounted for 32 percent of all shares traded in early dealing.
Dealers noted Telmex stock was moderating market gains by standing unchanged at brisk trade. The telecomms firm's L shares were flat at 18.64 pesos, while its ADRs were also unmoved at 46-7/8.
On the broad market, 43 stocks had changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered sliders by 21 to 10.
